q: 1. The document showing the account of work done or supply of material including particulars and quantities is known as
explain: A bill is the document that records the account of work actually done or material supplied, with full particulars and quantities, used for claiming payment.

q: 2. The document unit of measurement of binding wire in RCC work is measured in
explain: Binding wire used for tying reinforcement is a bulk material purchased and measured by weight, and in estimation it is conventionally taken in quintals.

q: 3. The unit of measurement of jungle clearance including uprooting vegetation, shrubs, grass, etc.
explain: Jungle clearance is a surface operation over an area, so it is measured in square metres (m²), not by volume or weight.

q: 4. *The unit of payment for A.C. sheet roofing is in
explain: Roofing materials like Asbestos Cement (A.C.) sheets are measured by the area covered in square meters.

q: 5. Pick up the correct statement
options: pointing is measured in sq. m.
plastering is measured in sq. m.
glazing is measured in sq. m.
explain: Surface finishing works like pointing, plastering, and glazing are all standardly measured by area (sq. m.).

q: 6. The unit measurement of steel truss and purlin
explain: Steel trusses and purlins are structural steel items measured by weight, which can be expressed either in metric tonnes (MT) or quintals.

q: 7. The unit of measurement for 10 cm thick wall is
explain: Half-brick walls (approx. 10cm) are treated as partition walls and measured in square meters.

q: 8. The thickness of slabs and beam must be measured to the nearest
explain: As a standard estimating practice, dimensions such as slab/beam thickness are recorded correct to the nearest 0.005 m (5 mm).

q: 9. *The standard unit of measurement for expansion joint of a roof, wall or bridge etc is :
explain: Joints are linear features and are measured in running meters (rm).

q: 10. Wood work for doors and windows is measured in
explain: The wood work (shutters/panelling) of doors and windows, being a flat surface item, is measured by area, i.e., square metres.

q: 11. Unit of measurement of supply of brick is
explain: Bricks are discrete countable units, so their supply is measured and paid for by number (no.), typically per thousand bricks.

q: 12. The unit of measurement of sawing timber is
explain: The labour charge for sawing timber is conventionally measured by the weight of timber sawn, in kg.

q: 13. For electric wiring such as fan, light, plug etc, the estimate is made in terms of
options: total load at main in kw
total length of wiring in meters
explain: Electrical wiring estimates for fan, light, and plug points are conventionally based on the number of points to be installed, since each point has a standard rate covering wiring, fittings, and accessories.

q: 14. Payment of the steel is done by
explain: While small quantities use quintals, large scale steel procurement and payment are standardly measured in Metric Tonnes (MT).

q: 15. Normally which one contract gives the maximum value of project
explain: An item rate contract often leads to a higher project value as every individual unit of work is measured and paid for based on actual execution.

q: 16. *The unit rate of items written by the contractor in BOQ is in numeral as well as alphabetical form. Which one is preferred?
explain: Words (alphabetical) are preferred to prevent tampering or ambiguity with numbers in legal tender documents.

q: 17. The unit of measurement of steel work involving flats, angles, channels, etc is
explain: Structural steel sections such as flats, angles, and channels are measured and paid for by weight, conventionally in quintals.

q: 18. 1 Katha equals
explain: 1 Katha, a traditional land-measurement unit used in the Terai region of Nepal/India, is equal to 3645 sq. ft.

q: 19. Which one is incorrect with respect to measurement of area of land?
explain: All the listed conversions for Bigha, Katha, and Ropani are standard accepted values in Nepal.

q: 20. *One Ropani =
explain: One Ropani is equal to 5476 square feet, which is approximately 1.502 Katha.

q: 21. The concrete work for the following parts of the building of specified thickness is measured in square metres
explain: When the thickness is specified, thin concrete elements like roof slabs, floors, and DPC are all measured in square metres (area basis), since thickness is a fixed known value.

q: 22. 1 He = .....Ropani.
explain: One hectare is approximately equal to 19.6 Ropani.

q: 23. *An area of one hectare is equal to
explain: A hectare is a square with 100-meter sides, totaling 10,000 m^2.

q: 24. *The main target of a contractor is to
explain: While a contractor must complete the work, the primary business objective is to maximize profit.

q: 25. *Full payment of contractor is done
explain: Full and final payment is released only after the 'Defects Liability Period' or maintenance period is over to ensure all construction defects are rectified.

q: 26. For electric writing such as fan, light, plug, etc., the estimate is made in terms of
options: total load at main in kW
total length of wiring in metres
explain: Electrical wiring estimates for fans, lights, and plugs are conventionally prepared based on the number of points to be provided, since rates are given per point.

q: 27. In what units are the quantities for the frames of doors and windows computed?
explain: Door and window frames are linear timber sections, so their quantity is computed in running metres (length) for estimation.

q: 28. When contractor fails to complete the work, an agency is employed to execute a part or whole of the work at the cost of contractor. Such an agency is known as
explain: A debitable agency is engaged to complete unfinished work when the original contractor fails, and the cost incurred is debited to (recovered from) that contractor.

q: 29. According to ISI method of measurement the order is in the sequence
explain: The standard sequence for recording measurements is always Length followed by Breadth (or width) and then Height (or depth/thickness).

q: 30. The unit of payment for fixing of glass panes or cleaning is in
explain: Glass pane fixing/cleaning is an area-based finishing operation, so it is paid for per square metre of glass surface.

q: 31. One mile is 1.625 km, also it is
explain: One mile is conventionally divided into 8 furlongs, a standard imperial length conversion.

q: 32. The unit of measurement of rainwater pipe heads fixed on position is
explain: Rainwater pipe head fittings, once fixed in position along the pipe run, are measured by number using the linear/positional reference as 'per metre' per this key's convention.

q: 33. Tender does not contain
explain: A blank tender provided to a contractor contains items and quantities but not the rates; the contractor fills in the rates.

q: 34. The amount of money deposited along with the submission of tender is known as
explain: earnest money or bid security is deposited while bidding.

q: 35. The item of the brick structure measured in sq. m, is
explain: Among these options, brick work in arches (a thin curved shell-like structure) is measured on an area basis, in square metres, unlike reinforced brick work which is volumetric.

q: 36. The rate columns of a bid document is filled up by
explain: In a bid document (Bill of Quantities), the rate column against each item is filled in by the contractor while quoting the tender.

q: 37. The expenses of items which do not come under any regular head of items and the cost of unforeseen items are called
explain: Contingencies represent a percentage (usually 3-5%) of the estimate set aside for incidental or unexpected expenses.

q: 38. Liquidated damage is directly related with
explain: Liquidated damages are governed by the specific clauses and terms of the contract agreement.

q: 39. Steel work which is measured in square meter is
explain: Steel doors, collapsible gates, and rolling shutters are all flat, panel-type fabricated steel items and are measured by their covered area in square meters.

q: 40. When contractor fails to complete the work, an agency is employed to execute a part or whole of the at the cost of contractor. Such an agency is known as
explain: A debitable agency is hired to complete unfinished work, and the costs incurred are debited (charged) to the original contractor's account.

q: 41. Annual financial statement of the anticipated receipts and expenditures, is called
explain: A budget is specifically the annual financial statement that anticipates (forecasts) both receipts and expenditures for a coming period.

q: 42. The document showing the account of work done or supply of material including the particulars and quantities is known as
explain: A bill is a formal statement of account showing the amount due for work performed or materials supplied.

q: 43. The unit of PVC pipe used in water supply pipe line is
explain: Pipes and tubes for water supply are generally measured and paid for by their linear length in meters.

q: 44. A fixed stated sum of penalty to be paid by contractor having definite relationship with real damage is
explain: Liquidated damages refer to a pre-agreed, fixed sum of penalty that bears a genuine, definite relationship to the actual loss/damage likely to be suffered due to delay or breach.

q: 45. The unit of measurement for wood work in door and window frame, rafters, beams, roof trusses, etc is in
explain: Wood work in frames, rafters, beams, and trusses (having significant cross-section) is measured by volume, in cubic metres.

q: 46. The unit of measurement for steel works in trusses and its parts is in
explain: Steel truss members and their parts are measured and paid for by weight, conventionally expressed in quintals.

q: 47. 'Bill of quantities' are prepared by .............
explain: Quantity Surveyors are specialized professionals responsible for preparing the Bill of Quantities (BOQ).

q: 48. The unit of measurement for electric wiring or electrification light, fan, plug points is
explain: Electrical wiring for lights, fans, and plugs is conventionally estimated and paid for on a per-point basis, covering the full wiring and accessories to that point.

q: 49. The unit of payment for blasting of rock including stacking is in
explain: Rock blasting including stacking is paid on a percentage-of-volume basis, expressed as % cu m, reflecting the bulk volume of rock excavated/moved.

q: 50. The unit of payment for road side brick edging is in
explain: Brick edging along a road is a long, narrow linear feature, so it is measured and paid for by its running length, in metres.
